title: Finite point internal-Hom evaluation comparison
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. For every $C\in D^b_{ctf}(s,A_n)$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], put $c=\operatorname{Fib}_s(C)$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and $\omega_{s,n}=Ra_s^!(A_n)_s$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The canonical evaluation-transpose map, formed using the point-fibre tensor and unit comparisons [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] and the derived sheaf internal Hom [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-pur-derived-internal-hom],
$$
\kappa_C:\operatorname{Fib}_s igl(R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(C,\omega_{s,n}) igr)\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(c,A_n),
$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $C$. The normalization $\omega_{s,n}\cong(A_n)_s$ is the following one: for $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$ with the identity compactification the etale compact support is the identity and its right adjoint is $a_s^	imes=\operatorname{id}$, so $\omega_{s,n}=
u_s^*R
u_{s,*}(A_n)_s$ for the comparison morphism $
u_s:s_{\mathrm{proet}}	o s_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and the normalization is the counit $
u_s^*R
u_{s,*}(A_n)_s	o(A_n)_s$, which is an isomorphism because $(A_n)_s=
u_s^*(A_n)_s$ and the unit $\operatorname{id}	o R
u_{s,*}
u_s^*$ is an isomorphism on bounded-below etale complexes [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. The map $\kappa_C$ is characterized by evaluation: after identifying $\omega_{s,n}\cong(A_n)_s$, the coefficient evaluation composed with $\kappa_C\otimes 1_c$ is the point-fibre of the sheaf evaluation.

source.place: Opening paragraph: at the identity point, the dualizing object is the coefficient unit and the displayed identification of D_s is the coefficient-module dual, computed by the derived internal Hom definition.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-finite-point-counit-unit-normalization] with the given finite-field and coefficient datum. It makes $A=A_n$ finite and identifies $\omega_{s,n}$ with $
u_s^*R
u_{s,*}(A_n)_s$ for the identity compactification. Its isomorphism $\alpha=\epsilon_{(A_n)_s}$ is precisely the normalization required here; its inverse is $
u_s^*(\eta_{(A_n)_{s,\mathrm{et}}})$.

source.place: Opening sentence: identity compact support and its right adjoint; finite comparison counit normalization (old item step 1).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-finite-point-reconstructed-hom-model] to the given bounded constructible $C$ and target $B=(A_n)_s$. It supplies exact realization and sections, $\Gamma B=A_n$, the natural reconstruction counit $e_C$, and the resolving-model isomorphism $Q_{C,B}$. Therefore $\beta_C=Q_{C,B}\circ\Gamma R\mathcal Hom(C,\alpha)$ is an isomorphism: its first factor is $Q_{C,B}$ and its second is the image of the isomorphism $\alpha$ under the derived Hom and sections functors. All objects and maps here are in the ambient derived categories.

source.place: Second sentence: compute point internal Hom over coefficients; exact realization, reconstruction and arbitrary-target resolution model (old item steps 2 and 3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-finite-point-reconstructed-evaluation-square] with $V=\omega_{s,n}$ and the specified $\alpha$. It puts $H=R\mathcal Hom(C,\omega_{s,n})$ in $D^b_{ctf}$, so the stipulated fibre tensor comparison is defined, and gives exactly $\operatorname{ev}_c(\beta_C\otimes1_c)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\alpha\operatorname{ev}_{C,V})\mu$. The same node identifies $\beta_C$ as the coefficient tensor-Hom transpose of that pairing, so the evaluation transpose $\kappa_C$ equals $\beta_C$. Thus it is invertible and has the required evaluation characterization. The derived naturality square in the same node, with the fixed $\alpha$ independent of $C$, gives the asserted contravariant naturality for every morphism $C\to C'$.

source.place: Second sentence: the displayed point-duality identification uses signed evaluation; reconstructed evaluation and derived naturality (old item steps 4 and 5).
